steps.title: Choose account types and delegated OAuth
steps.detail: Use delegated OAUTH2 for people connecting their own mailboxes; S2S_OAUTH2 is a separate application-permission path outside this guide. Choose single tenant for one organization, multitenant for business customers, and include personal accounts only if needed.

steps.title: Register your app in Microsoft Entra
steps.detail: Open Entra ID → App registrations → New registration, enter your app name and chosen account types, then save the Application (client) ID.

steps.title: Add the Web redirect and client credential
steps.detail: Under Authentication add a Web redirect matching your Composio auth config. Create a client secret for this supported flow and store its value securely; confirm the production credential approach with Composio because Microsoft recommends stronger alternatives.

steps.title: Set only the delegated permissions your tools need
steps.detail: Under API permissions choose Microsoft Graph delegated permissions: Mail.Read for reading, Mail.Send for sending, and Mail.ReadWrite only for mailbox changes. Keep offline_access for refresh; remove calendar, contacts and chat defaults unless your tools require them.

steps.title: Create a custom Outlook auth config
steps.detail: In Composio select Outlook OAUTH2 with your own credentials, enter the client ID/secret and chosen scopes, then use its auth config ID for Outlook sessions. Verify that the redirect exactly matches Entra.

steps.title: Complete publisher verification where needed
steps.detail: For multitenant business distribution, prepare the verified partner account and publisher domain and complete publisher verification. This improves trust and consent eligibility; it does not replace tenant approval.

steps.title: Resolve the customer tenant consent policy
steps.detail: Ask the tenant administrator to approve when the consent policy blocks the requested permissions; afterward have the original user start a fresh connection. Test this with each target tenant policy.

blocker.fix: Have its admin grant consent, then reconnect as the intended mailbox user.

steps.title: Connect the intended mailbox and test one tool
steps.detail: Connect your own mailbox through the Playground or a Connect Link and run a read operation first; verify send or change operations separately on test data. Reconnect users after a scope change.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Register an app in Entra ID > App registrations; choose single tenant, multiple tenants, or organizational plus personal accounts.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Publisher verification requires a verified Partner Program global account, a work/school app registration and a non-onmicrosoft.com publisher domain; eligible publishers can be verified in minutes. Risk-based consent can block new unverified multitenant apps.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Delegated mailbox consent depends on tenant policy; administrators can restrict user consent, including to verified publishers.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: For Needs Admin Approval, a tenant admin grants consent in API permissions or Enterprise applications, then the original user reconnects. Publisher verification does not override every tenant policy.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Delegated Mail.Read reads mail; Mail.ReadWrite modifies mail but does not send; Mail.Send sends. These delegated permissions do not inherently require admin consent, although tenant policies can.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: The live Outlook toolkit offers OAUTH2 and S2S_OAUTH2, managed OAUTH2, a client ID/secret custom flow, the Composio redirect URI and required offline_access. Its default scope set spans mail, calendar, contacts and chat.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: A server application registers its redirect URI using the Web platform in the Authentication settings.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: A client secret is created under Certificates & secrets; its value is displayed once. Microsoft recommends certificates or federated credentials for production.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Custom auth configs hold the provider client credentials and are selected through the session authConfigs mapping.

evidence.label: official
evidence.claim: Scope changes apply to new connections; existing users must reconnect to grant changed scopes.

evidence.label: unknown
evidence.claim: Certificate or federated-credential support in this Composio custom Outlook flow has not been established; the API currently requests a client secret.

access.note: Plan for publisher verification and tenant consent checks; a customer tenant may require its administrator to approve even a verified publisher.
